cells.tense: The cultivation is finished, and the shine now comes off what you made.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Look at the last few times something of yours landed. Trace the line running through them — not the details, the repeated shape. That shape is what carried the light.
cells.core:
You're in fog and it isn't costing what it used to. You see the next step and not much past it, and you take the step. What you built has reached the point where it gives off light while you sleep — you're not straining to be seen. That's why the shine holds. It isn't asking anything from you right now. It comes off the work the way warmth comes off a wall that's been in the sun.

Before you do anything else with it, look back. Take the last few times something of yours landed, and find the single line running underneath them — not the particulars, the part that repeated. Whatever carried the light before will carry it again, and once you see that line you can leave the fog unread. The line isn't a route to the next thing. One visible step and one clear pattern is enough to keep moving on.
cells.sheetLine: The light comes off what you made, not off your effort.
cells.verb: steering by the one light that's actually yours
cells.place: in the fog where one step shows and the next mile doesn't

cells.tense: You will have worked it out before it starts, and the brightness is arriving ahead of the thing.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Before you start the next one, wait until a single piece stands out as the piece that counts. Then begin with only that piece. The rest can hold.
cells.core:
The fog ahead is being lit by a shine that hasn't been earned yet — the version where it works, the moment it lands, the whole arc seen at once from a distance. It's bright enough to stun, and from inside you can't easily tell whether you're looking at hope or at dread. The future does the bracing for you, so the real work on your desk keeps getting outshone by a thing you can't write into. Dazzling and illuminating aren't the same.

Before you start the next one, wait. Let one piece come forward as the piece that counts, and begin there, without the whole plan lit up. If nothing separates itself, that's useful information — stay with it a while, because finding which piece counts takes the time it takes. You don't have to know why it counts. The thing to know is which piece to touch first, and to touch it.

cells.tense: You stood at that door, and you have since turned and walked away.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: For a week, keep something you used to care about alive in a form too small to fail. Ask nothing back — no progress, no verdict. Just fed.
cells.core:
The fog is no longer the trouble — you stopped watching for light in it. Something you were building toward ran long and didn't flower, and by now you've stopped standing at that door. From outside you look calm about it. From inside, nothing is pointed anywhere. The wish that started it is still on the record, and it's been sitting quiet a while.

Start smaller than feels serious. Take something you used to care about and give it a week in a form too small to fail — nothing asked back, no verdict, no watching for signs. Tend it the way you'd tend a young plant that doesn't owe you anything yet. The point isn't to get the light back on schedule. It's that when it returns, it finds something still being fed instead of a closed door. Being judged early is how it died the first time.

cells.tense: The light is coming off what you make already, and your own account leaves it out.
cells.act: stay standing in it a while longer
cells.ask: When the work starts to glow and you move to step aside or wave it off as luck, stand there a while longer. Don't explain it. Keep it yours.
cells.core:
You're radiating, and it hasn't landed that you're where it comes from. People come to you for the thing you make, and your own version has you still figuring it out, or credits the crew, the timing, the year. The shine was carried here by the same hand that kept showing up through the fog when quitting was easier — and your account of yourself leaves that hand out. The light is coming from the building, and you file it as reflection.

When the work starts to glow and you move to step aside, or wave it off as luck, stay where you are a little longer. Don't decide anything. Don't make a speech. Just stand in the light of something you made and keep it attached to you for the hour. Taking your name off it isn't modesty, and putting it on isn't boasting. It's accuracy — and accuracy is the whole ask.

cells.verb: steering by the one light that's actually yours
